notes.title: What's Going On
notes.notes:
[b]Corrosive Supporters[/b],

Hey everyone!

Just wanted to post a quick announcement to talk about what I've been up to.

Affliction, my current project is just about finished. It should only be another week or two, if all goes well.

I've been brainstorming hundreds of ideas for my next project which I will be starting almost immediately after Affliction is done because I'm so excited to work on it. I decided that I wanted to do a low-fantasy, medieval, open world role playing game with a massive scale. From my past role playing games, I'll take the knowledge that I've acquired, take the favorite features from them, and bring them back in a bigger, and better way. Of course, I'll be adding a lot of new stuff to the game too. I plan to make custom graphics for everything, get good sounds and music, and of course, create an enjoyable experience. It will be, by far, my largest project yet. I want to really go all-out with this. It will be flavored by the high medieval period of Western Europe and be sprinkled with low-fantasy and low-magic.

My current  inspirations are:
The Neverwinter Nights series
The Baldur's Gate series
Dungeons & Dragons
The Witcher series
The Stronghold series
The Medieval Total War series
The Mount & Blade Series
Chivalry: Medieval Warfare
Grim Dawn
The Black Death movie
The Ironclad movie series
The Lord of the Rings movie series
The Conan movie series
And MANY more...

I don't want to give too terribly many details right now, but hopefully some people will be excited about this next direction that I want to take.

If you'd like to donate and help me with this next project, the link can be found below. I truly do appreciate any and all donations as they help me pay for various pieces and parts needed for my game projects.

notes.title: 5/30/18 Development Status Update
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

So, I know it was just a few days ago that I posted one of these, but I wanted to post another to talk about some new content additions coming to Affliction.

If you read the previous dev log, you know that there have been new melee weapons added to increase variety and to allow players some say in what they take with them on their journey. Well, this is also the case for the shotgun. In addition to the Baikal MP153 shotgun, there will also be a Mossberg 590 Tactical shotgun in the game. The Mossberg does slightly more damage than the Baikal, has slightly reduced range, has slightly more recoil, packs a lot more of a punch, and is even better suited for CQB.

It will work the same way the melee weapons do in that if you have one shotgun, and find the other, you can simply trade them.

Yesterday was a pretty good day as far as map making goes as well. I finished up one map and then was able to start and complete an entirely new map. I really think players will enjoy these ones, as they add some new gameplay.

The main storyline for the game should be completed within the next few weeks and the game is nearing completion! It's been one heck of a trip with this game, but it's been a huge learning experience and a lot of fun. [b]Thank you to everyone who has accompanied me on this incredible road to building Affliction.[/b] My next game is probably going to return to my roots with another RPG theme, but I plan to make it bigger, better, and by far be the largest project I've done yet, combining all of my knowledge and skills.

I'll post more updates in the very near future. Stay tuned!

-[b]Eric "Corrosion" Plasencia[/b] :CStudios:

notes.title: 5/25/18 Development Status Update
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

Hey everybody!

So, I hope you've all been enjoying the latest update, but I wanted to stop by and let you in on what's in the works!

I decided it would be nice if players had a bit more choice in gameplay style, so I decided to add in some new melee weapons so they can choose what one they like best. Basically, there will be three different melee weapons. A combat knife, a metal pipe, and a sledge hammer. Now, the combat knife has been in the game all along, but the metal pipe and sledge hammer are new and have some unique traits. The knife is very fast and does a little damage. The pipe is slightly slower and does slightly more damage, and the sledge hammer is slow but does a lot of damage. Each weapon has it's own unique set of sound effects and animations, and it's own unique style of use and play. More weapons may come later in the future, too. Possibly even different gun variations.

When you have a melee weapon, you're free to swap that weapon for another. For instance, if you have a metal pipe and you see a sledge hammer lying on the ground, you'll simply replace the pipe with the hammer by using it. All the maps have now been updated and some of the places where knives spawned have been switched to the other weapons.

Chapter 6 - Aftermath has been coming along nicely, and has already brought some new content to the fray. New enemies, locations, and even some new gameplay aspects including challenges such as parkour levels and the "hellish nightmare" idea. Of course, there is still a lot of action! I plan to finish this chapter within the next few weeks!

Some bug fixes have also come into play such as some material mismatches with entities and some AI bugs, but most bugs are already taken care of.

That's all for now! Stay tuned for more information and updates in the near future!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] :CStudios:

notes.title: 4/9/18 Stealth System Development Status Update
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b]

Hey everyone!

So, as many of you know, the stealth system was a little lackluster in the game. This is no longer the case. 

Now, the AI can detect player movement within a small radius around them to check if the player is sneaking, moving, running, jumping, or walking. They will react accordingly.

Another change is the addition of their sight awareness for flashlight detection. If the player has their flashlight on and is within a certain distance, the AI will now react as if they are startled and begin trying to take the player down!

Further changes include extending the backstab range when attempting to sneak up behind an enemy to melee them, the AI now have slightly further distance of detection.

One side change to the AI is the addition of an ammo counter system so enemy characters will now need to reload every so often, too! Adding a whole new level of complexity and randomness to combat!

Numerous other changes to the AI have also been made but those were mainly adjustments and fine tuning.

The Stealth System update will come with the release of chapter 5 - Relapse. Coming soon! This update is going to be HUGE!

That's all for now!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

notes.title: 4/4/18 Development Status Update [Audio Overhaul]
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

Hey guys!

So, as many of you know, something has always been missing from Affliction. Immersion. The game lacks certain aspects and features that makes for great modern shooters. This should no longer be the case!

After several days of planning, organizing, and finally coding, the game now has a realistic and dynamic hit detection system directly linked to sound effects that can help add more depth and immersion to the combat, making it feel better and more satisfying.

There are several bullet ricochet, fly by, and crack sound effects that will play when the player is being shot at as well as several melee hit sound effects that will play if the player is hit by melee and even a miss sound if the player manages to dodge the attack!

These changes make the combat much more fulfilling and enjoyable!

The audio overhaul will come with the release of chapter 5 - Relapse!

That's all for now!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

notes.title: 2/1/18 Update 1.6 [AI Overhaul]
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28286649/da1b64bedf99760ca8418a436f0baba304ec2621.png[/img]

[i]You're afflicted now,
No longer in control,
No chance to stop it,
It's already taken hold...[/i]

Hey everyone! Here is the next major update for the game!

This update was supposed to be coupled with the release of Chapter 4, but the mapping is taking a little longer than planned, but that should be out within the next 2 weeks.

For now, here is the complete AI overhaul!

The AI in Affliction wasn't anything special... Now, that is no longer the case. Each aspect has been drastically improved and updated. Now, it's a fight! The AI wil be much more challenging and difficult to take down. They'll flank, evade, hunt, patrol, and do whatever it takes to bring down their prey.

Do you have what it takes? 

[b]Update 1.6 [AI Overhaul] Change Log:[/b]

Bug Fixes:
-Fixed a bug with nearly all special enemies freezing if they took damage while roaring/preparing to attack
-Fixed pathfinding bugs
-Fixed bugs with enemy damage range (enemies would do no damage if the player simply moved about a centimeter backwards while the npc was attacking)
-Fixed bugs with enemies automatically knowing the player location
-Fixed bugs with enemy attack/alert sound effects
-Various general fixes & improvements to code

Changes & Additions:
-Added "flicker" effect to flashlight when it dies
-Added constant pathfinding for the AI
-Added "unstuck" system so AI will continuously try to get themselves unstuck if they become stuck
-Tweaked AI shooting/target acquisition algorithm
-Added "personal bubbles" around the AI to avoid player/NPC physics getting tangled
-Revamped stealth mechanics with the AI reactions
-Added damage range increments to all AI
-Added "constant aggression" system to make the AI much more reactive in combat (before, they would lose track of the player and simply return to their idle state like nothing ever happened)
-Added "encounter" system to give the AI an area of influence where they will actively hunt the player
-Added "hunt" system so the AI now properly hunts the player in their environment if an encounter is triggered
-Added timers to all AI to make them more dynamic while in combat
-Added health increments for "flinching" for enemies (before they would just flinch every single time they took damage and that made them very easy to control and kill)
-Headshot damage calculation revamp
-Balanced some sound volume levels
-Adjusted some AI animations
-Improved AI (human gun wielding) enemy melee handling
-Added new documents to the Archives DLC

Chapter 4 will be released very soon! In the meantime, enjoy this AI overhaul!

Stay tuned for further updates and news in the future!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

The AI in Affliction wasn't anything special... Now, that is no longer the case. Each aspect has been drastically improved and updated. Now, it's a fight! The AI wil be much more challenging and difficult to take down. They'll flank, evade, hunt, patrol, and do whatever it takes to bring down their prey.

Do you have what it takes? 

[b]Update 1.6 [AI Overhaul] Change Log:[/b]

Bug Fixes:
-Fixed a bug with nearly all special enemies freezing if they took damage while roaring/preparing to attack
-Fixed pathfinding bugs
-Fixed bugs with enemy damage range (enemies would do no damage if the player simply moved about a centimeter backwards while the npc was attacking)
-Fixed bugs with enemies automatically knowing the player location
-Fixed bugs with enemy attack/alert sound effects
-Various general fixes & improvements to code

Changes & Additions:
-Added "flicker" effect to flashlight when it dies
-Added constant pathfinding for the AI
-Added "unstuck" system so AI will continuously try to get themselves unstuck if they become stuck
-Tweaked AI shooting/target acquisition algorithm
-Added "personal bubbles" around the AI to avoid player/NPC physics getting tangled
-Revamped stealth mechanics with the AI reactions
-Added damage range increments to all AI
-Added "constant aggression" system to make the AI much more reactive in combat (before, they would lose track of the player and simply return to their idle state like nothing ever happened)
-Added "encounter" system to give the AI an area of influence where they will actively hunt the player
-Added "hunt" system so the AI now properly hunts the player in their environment if an encounter is triggered
-Added timers to all AI to make them more dynamic while in combat
-Added health increments for "flinching" for enemies (before they would just flinch every single time they took damage and that made them very easy to control and kill)
-Headshot damage calculation revamp
-Balanced some sound volume levels
-Adjusted some AI animations
-Improved AI (human gun wielding) enemy melee handling
-Added new documents to the Archives DLC

Chapter 4 will be released very soon! In the meantime, enjoy this AI overhaul!

Stay tuned for further updates and news in the future!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] :CStudios:

notes.title: 12/22/17 Development Status Update [Complete AI Overhaul]
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28286649/da1b64bedf99760ca8418a436f0baba304ec2621.png[/img]

Hey again everyone!

So, I posted a status update yesterday in the middle of the day after having worked all morning but then I continued working late into the night on improving the AI.

After a few hours of solid coding, I can safely say that the next update will SIGNIFICANTLY improve the AI in every single way. Flanking, maneuvering, using cover, suppressive fire, constant target acquisition, and many more behaviors have been added for the human AI.

For the Afflicted (zombie type) AI, advanced tracking, sense of smell, constant target updates, and a few other behaviors have been added.

Sense of hearing has also been improved for all AI.

AI will no longer lose sight of the player and completely return to normal, like nothing ever happened. With a heightened alert system, area of influence for encounters, and more efficient algorithms for combat, the game should be much more fluid in playing.

Another issue that is fixed from this is the AI becoming stuck on obstacles. Since the old AI version only checked player location one time instead of constantly, AI would often get stuck on obstacles while moving toward the player. This should no longer be the case. They can get themselves unstuck now if this does happen.

The stealth system has also been improved. As I said above, there is now a heightened alert system that I custom wrote yesterday that makes the AI react much better to different events. Enemy AI also now have a small "area of influence" around them so you won't be able to escape their attempts to hunt you down so easily anymore.

This was a major breakthrough for the game. Truly. This major improvement will come with the release of chapter 4 and all of it's goodies. Coming soon.

I hope everyone is excited for the update!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

notes.title: 12/21/17 Development Status Update
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

Hey everyone!

Here's another quick status update to talk about progress being made on the game.

Over the past few days, the next map that takes place directly after the events in chapter 3 in the game has been completed. It came out pretty good and I can't wait to hear what people think. This is a much bigger map than many of the others currently in the game.

I've received a lot of feedback concerning the AI in the game and most of it has said they need to be improved. I agreed completely so another thing that I've been working on is improving it. I can now say that combat will be significantly more dynamic and the AI is much smarter and more realistic. Adding some extra event handling to their code has improved their effectiveness drastically.

Another topic that had a lot of feedback that kind of links to the AI was the fact that combat was too easy and the AI was not very challenging. Again, I agreed to this. Coupled with the AI improvements, I decided to completely remove instant kill headshots. It is still possible to kill an enemy in a single shot to the head, but you'll need a weapon that deals a lot of damage instead of being able to instant-kill anything you hit with any weapon in the head. Now, the damage done from headshots is changed from instantly depleting enemy health to 0 to now doing the weapon's damage +75 additional damage. Since the standard human npc enemy has 100 health, most weapons will still kill in a single headshot, but may add some extra dynamic combat situations where an extra shot or two is necessary.

A lot of work has gone into improving the way certain entities (objects) act and feel in the game. From simple things such as a tree all the way to advanced things such as buildings have had extensive work to make them act better in the game. Trees have had a lot of work done to make clipping and their physics obstacles be reduced and allow easier and more fluid movement around them. Buildings and many other entities have had material updates, some texture changes, physics improvements, and other sublte but important changes.

More work has gone into brainstorming interesting locations, scenes, and plot material for the storyline. There is a lot of plans and stuff in the process of being made and a lot more content is to come.

Stay tuned, as there will be a lot more news and updates to come!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

notes.title: Renegade Tabletop Tools System - Now Available
notes.notes:
[b]Corrosive Supporters[/b],

RTTS is now availble to purchase and use! It is currently on a launch discount for 10% off! Grab it while it lasts!

The Renegade Tabletop Tools System consists of two powerful, but very easy to use tools to aid in tabletop or net-based role-playing sessions.

You can get it here:
http://store.steampowered.com/app/760970/Renegade_Tabletop_Tools_System/

Renegade Dice Roller System:
-The Renegade Dice Roller System (RDRS) simply and effectively simulates rolling any number of dice with any number of sides, any modifiers, and will break down the mathematic equation results for you and display them for easy understanding. It also keeps a running total of which dice is being rolled and the grand total of all rolls combined. This can be used as a substitute for the chore of rolling real dice and help speed up combat, determining initiative, large scale battles, and much more!

Renegade Entity Dictionary System:
-The Renegade Entity Dictionary System (REDS) allows users to create and edit lists of entities, view lists, save lists as files, load list files, update list files, purge lists, and even retrieve a random entity from a list. This can be used to create lists of different game elements for nearly any gameplay aspect including loot, adventure, time, weather, location, enemies, and so much more! The sky is the limit!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

notes.title: 12/1/17 Development Status Report
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

Hey everyone!

As many of you know, I'm currently working on the next chapter's maps and storyline for the game along with numerous other things such as new weapons, enemies, and improving everything already in the game. 

Things have been kind of slow the past few weeks with the holidays, finals in my classes for college, and other various things that have required my attention. I'm pleased to say that will no longer be the case after next week, but as of today, I made a ton of progress on the game.

I've been trying to decide exactly what path I want the PC (Player Character) to take next and I think I've finally come up with the next part in the storyline and I feel it will be a good one. My pen and paper have been going non stop!

Most of my day was spent configuring/adjusting entities that I plan to use in the game at a later point, but a lot of work went into the next map and this will be a big one! It has a lot of atmosphere and great scenery. More pictures will be posted soon! Another thing I worked on today was resolving some strange AI behavior and adding "personal bubbles" around the player and all AI characters to avoid issues with clipping and getting stuck. I've heard a lot of feedback about the AI and I'm putting a lot of work into improving it and making it more realistic. Some other various things were fixed today including some material issues with certain entities, sound effect issues, some clipping errors, and a few other things.

Work will be in full swing again and much faster once all of my college classes are finished for this semester. Should only be another week and I'll be ready to attentively work on the game! The next update will be out soon after!

Hope you're looking forward to it!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

The Renegade Tabletop Tools System consists of two very easy to use tools to aid in tabletop role-playing sessions.

Renegade Dice Roller System:
-The Renegade Dice Roller System (RDRS) simply and effectively simulates rolling any number of dice with any number of sides, any modifiers, and will break down the mathematic equation results for you and display them for easy understanding. It also keeps a running total of which dice is being rolled and the grand total of all rolls combined. This can be used as a substitute for the chore of rolling real dice and help speed up combat, determining initiative, large scale battles, and much more!

Renegade Entity Dictionary System:
-The Renegade Entity Dictionary System (REDS) allows users to create and edit lists of entities, view lists, save lists as files, load list files, update list files, purge lists, and even retrieve a random entity from a list. This can be used to create lists of different game elements for nearly any gameplay aspect including loot, adventure, time, weather, location, enemies, and so much more! The sky is the limit!

notes.title: 11/10/17 Update 1.4 [Immersion Update]
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

Hey everyone, as promised, here is our second public update and we've brought a ton of changes and improvements that have been mentioned and requested by the community! We have heard your words, and we've come to deliver.

The biggest changes in this update have to do with sound effects and the HUD (Heads Up Display) and focus on improving the game to be more realistic. The HUD was just a placeholder for the time and will now be much more elaborate. Another big change is a complete animation overhaul for several enemies. More of these types of changes will be seen in the future.

A lot of other work has been done on our end that will be coming in the future such as creating new enemy types, weapons, and other entities to give the game more variety. We have a lot of different ideas and plans on how everything will all come together and we believe it will be interesting to see everything unfold.

[b]Update 1.4 [Immersion Update] Change Log:[/b]

Bug Fixes:
-Fixed Credits page back button being in the way on some text
-Fixed a few clipping entities
-Moved some entities that caused AI to get stuck
-Fixed some entities not being the correct material

Changes & Additions:
-Increased brightness on all Triglav Facility maps
-All weapon handling sound effects have been updated
-Jump sound effect updated
-Removed a few excess enemies
-Added a few more pick ups to several maps
-Added some new areas to a few maps
-Flashlight death time increased by 5 seconds (now it will die between 35 seconds to 180 seconds)
-Animations updated for several enemies
-HUD information updated and custom for each individual weapon
-HUD will now display ammo type for the currently held weapon
-AK47 renamed to AKM
-Makarov renamed to Makarov PM
-Makarov Ammo renamed to 9x18mm PM Rounds
-MP153 Baikal Ammo renamed to 12x70mm Buckshot Shells
-Agram 2000 Ammo renamed to 9x19mm Parabellum Rounds
-AK47 Ammo renamed to 7.62x39mm Soviet Rounds
-Dragunov Ammo renamed to 7.62x54mm R Rounds
-Slight balance modifications done to all weapons
-Adjusted some enemy stats
-Moved a few enemy spawns
-Moved several pick up spawns
-Changed some text popup contents
-Adjusted lighting/color effects in all maps
-Added some more ambient sound effects

[u]PLEASE NOTE: THIS UPDATE MAY REQUIRE A NEW SAVE GAME. SORRY FOR ANY INCONVENIENCE THIS MAY CAUSE.[/u]

The update will be live shortly.

The community poll determined that a standard crosshair will not be added to the game. However, in the coming future, new weapons will be added that will make this change "unnecessary". We'll tell you exactly what we mean by that soon.

The next update will take some time, but will feature more gameplay and more new content. Please be patient, the wait will be worth it!

[b]What Now?:[/b]
[spoiler]The journey ahead of Vasya is a long and dangerous one. It is full of hardship and misery. Agony, and death. What lies ahead is unknown to him, but perhaps it is fate that guides his steps...

If you had the power to decide, where could Vasya go next in his story? Feel free to post your ideas below! You could help shape Vasya's future and the future of the entire game![/spoiler]

If there are any bugs or problems, please report them in the appropriate forum on the community hub!

Enjoy!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

notes.title: Affliction - 11/5/17 Status Update/Crosshair Poll
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

Hello there everyone!

Hope you're enjoying the game so far, even in it's current early stages. 

Work continues to improve the game in various ways and I wanted to take the time to talk about some upcoming changes and improvements with the next update.

One thing that I got a lot of feedback about was the HUD system and it's very basic information. For example, the HUD would display "rifle" when holding an AK47/AKM. This was a placeholder for the time. The next update will display actual weapon names for all of the weapons on the HUD, display the correct ammunition type and image.

The AK47 has been renamed to "AKM" as the actual AK47 is no longer in service by any modernized country. The AKM is a modernized version of the AK47 for those of you that do not know.

The Makarov has been renamed to "Makarov PM". The PM literally stands for Pistolet Makarova - Makarov Pistol. Even though it is technically already in the name, this is the proper designation.

All ammunition in the game is now completely technically correct and will display how much you get when picking it up. Changes are displayed below:

Old - New
AK47 Ammo - 7.62x39mm Soviet Rounds
Agram 2000 Ammo - 9x19mm Parabellum Rounds
Makarov Ammo - 9x18mm PM Rounds
Baikal MP 153 Shells - 12x70mm Buckshot Shells
SVD Dragunov Ammo - 7.62x54mm R Rounds

Another major change is the addition of a crosshair. If any crosshair is added, it will be very simple and small. The game is meant to be slightly difficult and slightly more realistic in terms of combat mechanics, so Iron Sights are encouraged to use, but if the community wants a crosshair, it may be added. This may or may not happen depending on the poll which can be taken here: https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/K27LFTZ

All of the maps that take place in the Triglav facility have been brightened up so they aren't so dark. That was a problem and it is now fixed for the next update.

The credits screen has been updated so that the button is not in the way of any of the text.

New maps and further story sections will be coming soon too, so stay tuned for more information on all of that. The Dragunov SVD will be available to use starting in Chapter 4, so that is something to look forward to. Many more enemies types will also be added!

I really want the game to feel "good" when playing it. I want it to draw people in and the story to be captivating. I want to make the game feel more interactive and less linear too. I'm going to do my best to expand it and do all of this.

Now, this is a possible feature to be added, but I may even do full voice overs for the main character whenever he speaks or thinks something. Currently, it just displays text at the bottom of the screen and gives a notification sound effect. This may or may not be added in the future. To go with this though, all actor sound effects would be updated from what they currently are as of right now.

The last few days have been very busy for me, but I plan to get a lot more work done this week and hopefully release the next update for the game. All in due time.

Feel free to post questions or comments here, as I'll be monitoring this announcement for feedback.

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

notes.title: 10/27/17 Update 1.3
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

Hello everyone! This is the first public update for [i]Affliction[/i]! We've got a few changes based on community feedback along with several bug fixes. Many more patches and updates will be coming soon!

The biggest change with this patch is in the graphics, lighting, and color system. We originally intended to render the game in a Cell Shader style similar to Borderlands or a comic book, and now it is! We've also made numerous adjustments to the color scheme of the game and the lighting system to really give the graphics a "pop".

[b]Update 1.3 Change Log:[/b]

Bug Fixes:
-Fixed "ghost papers" that clipped into the desk in map3 (lowerlabs)
-Fixed enemy clipping issues on several maps
-Fixed a bandage that couldn't be used on map7 (forest)
-Reformatted the exe files for the game to properly display the game name as the process

Changes & Additions:
-Enabled "Cell Shader" graphical effect (Comic Book Art Style)
-Adjusted lighting and shadow effects
-Tweaked colors of all environments
-Added a slight vignette effect around the screen
-Adjusted base FOV (Field of View) (+5)
-Adjusted weapon FOV (Field of View) (+3)
-Greatly increased the size of all notes/documents (+140p W, +183p H)
-Increased brightness of subtitles and hint text
-Made the first level's path much more obvious
-Altered spawning system for multiple enemies across all maps
-Moved several props that caused the AI to become stuck
-Adjusted AI reaction time slightly
-Increased all interaction ranges slightly
-Removed some extra entities on all maps to help with load times
-Rewrote some help tips and message pop ups
-Removed collision and physics on several distant (background) objects to increase FPS (Frames Per Second)

In case you missed the post earlier, you can see the different graphical effects here:

Pre Shader:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28286649/6a78fdd16a9e24a6bb51ba729638b94b3f0c20ca.jpg[/img]

Post Shader:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28286649/7ccea2bca37d76cb32b5a5fabe6960f1dff9b3b1.jpg[/img]

Remember to save often just in case of game breaking issues! This is still a work in progress and Early Access!

[u]PLEASE NOTE: OLD SAVES MAY OR MAY NOT WORK WITH THE NEW VERSION OF THE GAME. SORRY FOR ANY INCONVENIENCE THIS MAY HAVE CAUSED. THIS WILL ONLY HAPPEN THROUGHOUT THE EARLY ACCESS PHASE OF THE GAME.[/u]

Thanks you everyone who has shown their support and interest in the project! Your help is truly appreciated! We wouldn't be here without you!

Enjoy!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

notes.title: Affliction - Post Release Status Update
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

Hello everyone!

I've been listening to the community over the past few days and hard at work to improve on and fix issues currently present in the game. I would like to push out the first patch this weekend at some point and then proceed to start working on more content for the game. A lot of the bugs that I have come across and have had reported to me are small for the most part and have already been fixed and will be patched within the next few days.

After talking to some individuals in the community and seeing what some others have had to say, I've removed the RPG tag from the game page as it doesn't seem to fit. There are some light rpg elements, but not enough to classify this as an rpg. It is, in all senses, an fps game with horror and rpg elements. It's a shooter and a combat game.

notes.title: Affliction - Now Available
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28286649/c6bf2a3e528355788c1ff8eeeb45ac525070a41b.png[/img]

The time has come for [i]Affliction[/i] to be released into Early Access!

You can check it out here: http://store.steampowered.com/app/617590/Affliction/

Set in the fictional Eastern European country of Ghulovka, amidst a terrible civil war, Affliction allows players to take on the role of Vasya, a patient plagued by nightmares and fractured memories, who awakes inside of a cell in a bizarre research facility where grim human experiments are taking place. With no memory of their reason for being there, players are forced to fight for their survival amidst a hellish catastrophe while frantically seeking answers to discover the truth behind their identity and unveil the mystery surrounding the horrific true purpose of the complex.

Venture into the Triglav Complex: an abandoned, cold war era, soviet military research base whose original purpose involved developmental weapons. Now, the derelict compound is operating once again with similar intent. A dreadfully dangerous and highly classified chemical weapon known only as Morana has been under design for years, but has become too difficult to control and containment has been breached. Affliction is a survival horror game designed to engage players with a thrilling storyline, surreal lore, sprawling environments, merciless foes, a chilling atmosphere, and an unforgettable gameplay experience. Players must explore, scavenge, and fight in order to survive and live to tell the tale.

Experience the terrifying possibilities of human experimentation, biological warfare, and chemical warfare from a first person perspective. The game features many different locations to explore including a disturbing research facility, a dark wilderness, a desolate city, and more. Exploration can be rewarding, but it can also be very unforgiving.

Adapt and use extreme caution with every choice made as there are also many different types of enemies who will bring a grisly demise to anyone foolish enough to underestimate them. Military death squads tasked to purge, ghastly mutants hunting to feed, and renegade anarchists attempting to resist are only some of the many hazards that await in this afflicted story.

[u]PLEASE NOTE: Affliction is currently in Early Access and will be for some time. Please only buy the game if you want to support us as a team and help us create a better game. There will be bugs, long loading times, crashes, progress resets, and other miscellaneous issues. We plan to solve all of these before final release to deliver a polished and fun experience but for now, some may not want to deal with this. The price is reduced until final release to compensate in the meantime, but it is recommended to wait to purchase this game if you don't want to deal with issues that may be currently present.[/u]

notes.title: Affliction - Release Date Announcement
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28286649/b54f024ee0cff105e9c630526132127684905c51.png[/img]

The time has come to talk about the initial release of [i]Affliction[/i]!

[b][u]Our planned release date is Wednesday, the 25th of October - 10/25/17![/u][/b] Happy (early) Halloween!

As many of you know, the game will be in [b]Early Access[/b] for several more months until it is finally finished. A [u]ton[/u] of more gameplay content is planned as as with our previous games, [u]will[/u] be delivered.

There will be bugs, crashes, errors, loss of progress, and various other issues along the way. These issues are more likely to happen when the game is first released, but it is possible they will continue throughout the Early Access duration. [u]Please do not purchase the game for the time being, if you are not willing to deal with the issues listed above.[/u] If you want to support us, help us make a better game, and get the game at a huge (half price) discount, buy the game at your earliest convenience.

The game will be $6.99 upon initial (Alpha) release and is planned to be priced according to the amount of content and polish you receive. We did this with our previous titles and it was quite beneficial to both the players and ourselves. At the Beta phase, it is planned to be priced at $8.99. Upon final release, it will be $10.99. The earlier you purchase the game (and pledge your support by doing so) the less you have to pay for it.

Upon initial release, the game will feature the tutorial, introduction, the first three chapters, and a unique gameplay experience. There are multiple weapons, various factions, numerous enemies, lots of lore and story elements, gripping sound effects, completely original soundtracks, and large hand crafted environments.

To see exactly what will come in the initial release and future updates for the game, please look here: http://steamcommunity.com/app/617590/discussions/0/1474221865183892053/
This thread will be updated whenever a new update featuring new content is released.

Everything you'll see and experience in the game is customized and redesigned to fit into the game world. We believe that some of the best ideas come from the most untapped (and often strange) corners of creation. We want to put them to use! If anyone has anything they'd like to see in the game or have any ideas, share them! That's what Early Access is all about!

I know I personally can't wait to see what everyone thinks, and everyone else who is apart of Corrosive Studios is too! We hope you all are too!

notes.title: Affliction - 10/13/17 Status Update
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

Here's another quick status update!

We've finished our self testing and have made several changes as well as additions to the game.

One of our biggest changes regards the physics system. Right now, we've added a very simple system that allows you to pick up and move certain objects around to help with certain sections of the game. For example: you may need to move a box or crate to help you get over something. Objects that can be moved are labeled when you get close enough for easy recognition. In the future, more of these will be added and probably used for simple puzzles. We were quite unsure about how the physics system would handle this but to our surprise, it works very well.

We've fine tuned the "Last Chance" system that I announced a few days ago and we think it works really well now. The conditions have been modified with some special effects so it will really feel like you're fighting for your life.

We've added several more health item pick ups to the game as we felt before that they were too rare.

Ammo was found to be a little too plentiful in some areas, so some of the pick ups for that have been removed or have had their quantity lowered.

We're re-enabled text pop ups when you're near items to help players out by telling them what can be interacted with and what cannot. Note that this is only for item pick ups and weapons. This is not for doors and interaction objects.

We've added more enemies to the game to make it feel like more of a shooter with RPG elements instead of an RPG with shooter elements. That is the way it is intended to be. Think of games such as Cry of Fear, Silent Hill, The Evil Within, Singularity, Dead Space, Resident Evil, Doom, and so on.

The enemy health system has been tweaked for certain enemies so that some are more difficult than others (as intended) and need different tactics to be taken down. Of course, a ton of lead will still do the trick in any case. ;-)

Brightness and contrast in the game has been adjusted to make the game a bit brighter as in our testing we found that the game was a bit too dark. Now, it should be bright enough to see and interact without issue, but still give off the spooky feeling of being alone in the darkness.

Cinematics have had some work done to them as well. Before, they were a little sloppy and rushed but they were merely placeholders for the time being. Now, they are much more atmospheric and carefully done.

I fully expect that within the next few days, the public build will be uploaded to Steam and then after Valve checks it out, it will be released!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

notes.title: Affliction - 10/10/17 Status Update
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

Hey everyone, here's another quick status update regarding our progress with the game. ːAflashlightː

I wanted to talk about a new feature that I added today and go over how it works. Something I dubbed the [b]"Last Chance"[/b] system. ːAbandagesː

Basically it works like this: When you have 100 health, you'll be given the "Last Chance". It will display on your HUD (Heads Up Display) as a big "1" next to a damaged heart. When you reach 35 health or below, that 1 will change to a "0" and you'll lose the "Last Chance" temporarily, but you'll be given an additional 15 health (may change in the future based on feedback) to give you one last chance - hence the name - to save yourself. Now, the only way to get that "Last Chance" back is to reach 100 health again and fully recover. The player has a natural health regeneration of 1 health every 15 seconds (again, this may also change in the future based on feedback) so it's possible to regain this "Last Chance" without needing to find medical items like medical kits and bandages but it'll take some time. This helps encourage using cover and cutting back on the whole "run n gun" mentality. This game is not meant for that. [u]It is possible you won't always actually get a "Last Chance" because some weapons are more than capable of doing large amounts of damage in an instant.[/u] For example, the Dragunov SVD sniper rifle. That is a powerhouse of a weapon and very dangerous. It could (in some cases)  potentially do enough damage to lower you past the point where you'd lose the "Last Chance" and regain some health but still kill you. We're aware of this, and that is how it is meant to be. Enemies and the player do the same amount of damage. There are no handicaps on the NPCs. [u]The player will need to be smart in how they engage enemies and pick their fights wisely.[/u] ːArifleː

The addition of this feature also fixes an annoyance (not really a bug but something that didn't completely act the way we wanted) - the lives counter. With the engine that we chose to use, there is a hard coded (unchangable) feature that displays how many lives you have on your HUD. Since the game is realistic, you only have 1 life. So, it reminded you that you always have 1 life only which was pointless. Now, we've combined the lives system with the "Last Chance" system so now you know when you have that reserve "Last Chance" and when you do not. ːAsyringeː

Another thing we've worked on is getting the load times down and we've had great success. We previously had load times of over several minutes in length for a short and simple map, now they take between 10 and 30 seconds only. That is a tenth of our previous load times. We've also been able to increase the quality of the graphics all while still keeping performance good and stable. The game is really starting to take form and be capable of showing the true potential that it has. ːAmagazineː

Let me know what you guys think! We want feedback! ːWWFAKː

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

[u]It is possible you won't always actually get a "Last Chance" because some weapons are more than capable of doing large amounts of damage in an instant.[/u] For example, the Dragunov SVD sniper rifle. That is a powerhouse of a weapon and very dangerous. It could (in some cases)  potentially do enough damage to lower you past the point where you'd lose the "Last Chance" and regain some health but still kill you. We're aware of this, and that is how it is meant to be. Enemies and the player do the same amount of damage. There are no handicaps on the NPCs. [u]The player will need to be smart in how they engage enemies and pick their fights wisely.[/u] :Arifle:

The addition of this feature also fixes an annoyance (not really a bug but something that didn't completely act the way we wanted) - the lives counter. With the engine that we chose to use, there is a hard coded (unchangable) feature that displays how many lives you have on your HUD. Since the game is realistic, you only have 1 life. So, it reminded you that you always have 1 life only which was pointless. Now, we've combined the lives system with the "Last Chance" system so now you know when you have that reserve "Last Chance" and when you do not. :Asyringe:

Another thing we've worked on is getting the load times down and we've had great success. We previously had load times of over several minutes in length for a short and simple map, now they take between 10 and 30 seconds only. That is a tenth of our previous load times. We've also been able to increase the quality of the graphics all while still keeping performance good and stable. The game is really starting to take form and be capable of showing the true potential that it has. :Amagazine:

Let me know what you guys think! We want feedback! :WWFAK:

-[b]Corrosion[/b] :CStudios:

notes.title: Affliction - In Preparation for Release
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28286649/b54f024ee0cff105e9c630526132127684905c51.png[/img]

Hello everyone!

Currently, we're prepping the game for release. We've been testing nonstop and fixing bugs, polishing, reducing load times and clutter, and doing everything we can to ensure that release will be as smooth as possible. We've fixed several major bugs and errors that caused the game to be pretty much unplayable and we're confident now that the game is in good enough shape to ship out to Steam. While we cannot give an exact date, please understand that it is this way for a reason. The reason being polish. Please also keep in mind that Affliction will be in Early Access for some time and it is currently in late alpha stages of development. Most of the work we've got left to do will be an absolute huge amount of mapping, some cinematics, some small puzzles, and work on the storyline. The core systems are pretty much all good to go.

There is significantly more content that will be released initially than previously planned so that is why it took a little longer than expected but more content is a plus. You can see what the game has to offer currently, here: http://steamcommunity.com/app/617590/discussions/0/1474221865183892053/
The thread listed above will be updated as development progresses. The content viewed in this thread is likely to double, triple, or even quadruple in size as time goes on. There is a lot of content planned.

I plan to upload the build to Steam within the next few days (if all goes well in testing) to then have our designated Steam testers try it out. Shortly after that, the game is planned to be released and it will be in perfect timing for Halloween! :-)

As stated before, the game will receive updates and patches as soon as possible, but take in mind that working with 3D is a lot different than working with 2D so updates will likely be every couple of months but there will be a stable line of communication with me (Corrosion) directly on the Steam Community Hub for the game. I'll also be posting announcements constantly to showcase our work.

Last but not least, thank you. Thank you to everyone who has believed in the project and helped it come to life, you'll soon be able to see what you helped create!

notes.title: 9/30/17 Affliction Development Status Update
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

So, it's been awhile since I posted an announcement regarding the progress of development with Affliction. Worry not, as development has continued and in fact, has been going relatively smoothly.

I completely redesigned the intro to the game. Before, it was kind of sloppily put together and didn't feel "fluid" when play testing. The new version will come with several maps and different segments. It will also contain much more lore (early game background info) and more combat. It will also help new players by easing into the combat more smoothly as combat is and always will be difficult.

I (again) redesigned the HUD and have continued to improve the functionality of the interaction system.

AI continues to improve slowly but surely by increasing aggression and reaction.

As soon as I finish up redesigning the intro, I plan to release Affliction for Early Access. 

The game is planned to be priced at $6.99 upon initial release and will launch with a week long 10% discount.

Last but not least, I wanted to give a huge thanks to everyone who has believed in us and supported our past projects as well as this one so far. We truly wouldn't be here without you guys! I have a lot of plans and see a lot of potential in this project. I hope you guys feel the same and join me to create another fantastic game!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

notes.title: Affliction - Hurricane Harvey Relief Effort
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

As many of you are well aware, Hurricane Harvey devastated many of the southern coastal states. As a Texas resident myself, I saw some of it first hand.

For the month of September, I plan to donate a large percentage of all profits from Waste Walkers to the relief effort. If you'd like to help out, please continue to read.

I'm asking anyone and everyone who'd like to help support the victims of the storm, to please purchase Waste Walkers or any of it's DLCs to help those in need. Every little bit helps no matter how little you may spend. 

I've taken it upon myself with my family to personally send supplies including food, clothing, pet food, baby supplies, medical supplies, clean water, and other various items to help out the survivors living in chaos.

A lot of people either have ignored the issue or have not heard of how bad it is for not only Houston, but the surrounding towns and neighboring cities. Even other states.

Don't do this for me or my business, think of the people who could use the money to help them get their lives back on track. Think of how you'd feel in their situation. You'd probably need some help and feel very appreciative of any donations or help received.

Please, if you're able, help me do what's right.

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

notes.title: Affliction - Unplanned Content Addition - "Basic"
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

So, as it's been said several times, the game will be difficult and won't be holding any hands. It is being built this way on purpose but, I decided today that it might be a little bit more fair to have a very simple tutorial. It won't be part of the main game however. The main game is supposed to have a "shock factor" for its first scene and the skill required to succeed. This should last throughout the game. Now, it won't be ridiculous for difficulty, but it should be somewhat challenging for the average player. The game is both a shooter and a thriller so combat shouldn't be all "run and gun and repeat".

This wasn't anticipated, and it certainly wasn't planned, but I had a change of heart late last night so all day today (from the moment I woke up this morning until writing this) I put together an old military base that is fully functional in terms of a basic training tutorial, all while keeping with the same extreme atmosphere. With fully voiced speech lines and some deeply scripted elements, the tutorial will release [u]FOR FREE[/u] with the main game as a separate executable file upon release for all customers.

[u]It will go over several main game elements including self driven exploration, following orders, basic to advanced movement techniques, basic puzzle solving, basic item hunting and retrieval, item handling, basic weapon handling, and last but certainly not least wound recovery.[/u]

Veteran players of FPS style games won't need to do it and probably won't really learn anything new, but it may be fun to play through just for the experience and the continued amount of game play it offers for [i]Affliction[/i].

New players to FPS style games are encouraged to play through the tutorial but not required. That's why it is a completely separate executable file. I wanted to give the players complete choice over their individual participation in it.

Like I said above, it's a simple tutorial, but it's definitely going to be helpful to players and maybe even interesting to some.

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

notes.title: Affliction - Release Details
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28286649/b54f024ee0cff105e9c630526132127684905c51.png[/img]

Okay, so as many of you know, the game has been under development for a very long time already. It will continue to be this way so there is an absolute abundance of game play. I've taken care of most of the core mechanics in the game already, but things are subject to change especially if the community wishes it. As of this moment, there are 9 maps in the game that form 2 chapters. Upon release, it is planned that there will be 11 maps and they form 2 complete chapters and should offer a few hours of game play. Depending on play style, game play time may vary but in the future there will be a ton of maps and chapters so it shouldn't be an issue. There will probably be something like several dozen maps that combine to form several chapters. Don't quote me on those numbers exactly, but I want the game to offer a lot of play time.

Now, for some reason, with this game, whenever I try to upload a build to Steam over top of a pre existing build, it doesn't fully update. So, there will be times during Early Access where for part of a day, the game may be updated several times and there may be times when the game isn't playable for a few hours. Believe me, I will do everything I can to get it sorted as soon as possible just as I've done in the past with previous projects. I pay very close attention to the issues and bugs my games have and take care of them as soon and as best I can.

On to release details. I have definite plans to release the game very soon. Another month at the most unless something drastic takes place. I've been working on it every single day and pulling all nighters so I'm literally going as fast as I can. I know a lot of people are eagerly awaiting the release. I just want to finish up the last 2 maps for chapter 2 so that players get 2 full chapters to play, their money's worth, and have enough to do in the first Early Access release. The DLCs will also be released with the game so if anyone wishes to help us out and support is a bit more than average and get some neat stuff, please do. All the DLCs are just additional content and purely optional.

Updates will not be as often or numerous as with my previous titles. They will be less often, but MUCH BIGGER and offer a lot more content additions and changes. This will also give the community a lot of time to be able to contribute ideas and so on.

Please stay tuned! I hope you're all just as excited as we are at Corrosive Studios!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

notes.title: Affliction - Quick Look at Enemies (Spoilers)
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28286649/b54f024ee0cff105e9c630526132127684905c51.png[/img]

Hello everyone, I realize it's been awhile since I posted an announcement but I had to take a trip. I'm back now and ready to continue working!

So, I have quite a few enemies already in the game but I wanted to post some of them to see what you all think about them and see if anyone had anymore ideas they wanted to see in the game or modifications made. There are minor spoilers in this post.

Human enemies will have varying degrees of training, speed, health, accuracy, and armor. I'm not going to list all the human classes as it would be way too many and ruin game immersion.

Afflicted are listed below one at a time.

Ghoul
The ghoul has average health and moves somewhat slow. It's strengths are increased vision/scent range and slightly increased field of view.

Wretch
The wretch is a fast moving, extremely agile foe. It has only slight mutations so it retains a very human appearance. It is very weak, but does a lot of damage, quickly.

Ghast
The ghast is a heavily mutated human being that has undergone drastic changes to its genetic makeup. It is fast, resistant to damage, and able to deal a lot of damage in a short amount of time. It has increased vision/scent range but it's field of view is fairly low.

Wight
The wight is a slow but very strong mutated person. It has a high field of view and vision/scent range. It deals very high damage and can take a lot of punishment before falling.

Tweeker
The tweeker is very similar to the wight, but it is much faster and harder to hit as it tweeks and jerks uncontrollably.

Common Afflicted
The common afflicted are very much like zombies. They retain their human appearance and traits but have a lust for blood and will stop at nothing to satisfy it.

Deranged
The deranged are another form of the common afflicted. They are just slightly more resistant to damage, and can use basic tools as weapons. They are mostly slow and not very intelligent.

Mongrel
The mongrel was a biogenetically altered creature that was an old Soviet project, revitalized by the authorities of the Triglav Complex. It is a mix of a human and a gene modified wolf. It is fast, damage resistant, and deals damage at a very high rate. It also has high vision/scent range but suffers from a very low field of view as it has very low peripheral vision.

Invalid
The invalid are the test subjects for the various human experiments at the Triglav Complex. They are slow, average in health, have low field of view and sight/scent distances. They are sickened by various illnesses and driven insane due to torture and numerous operations.

Most of the afflicted have several variants with varied stats and appearances.

This is not a complete list, but this gives everyone a look at what we have been working with so far. Please let us know what you think.

notes.title: Affliction - Quick Look at Enemies (Spoilers)
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28286649/b54f024ee0cff105e9c630526132127684905c51.png[/img]

Hello everyone, I realize it's been awhile since I posted an announcement but I had to take a trip. I'm back now and ready to continue working!

So, I have quite a few enemies already in the game but I wanted to post some of them to see what you all think about them and see if anyone had anymore ideas they wanted to see in the game or modifications made. There are minor spoilers in this post.

Human enemies will have varying degrees of training, speed, health, accuracy, and armor. I'm not going to list all the human classes as it would be way too many and ruin game immersion.

Afflicted are listed below one at a time.

Ghoul
The ghoul has average health and moves somewhat slow. It's strengths are increased vision/scent range and slightly increased field of view.

Wretch
The wretch is a fast moving, extremely agile foe. It has only slight mutations so it retains a very human appearance. It is very weak, but does a lot of damage, quickly.

Ghast
The ghast is a heavily mutated human being that has undergone drastic changes to its genetic makeup. It is fast, resistant to damage, and able to deal a lot of damage in a short amount of time. It has increased vision/scent range but it's field of view is fairly low.

Wight
The wight is a slow but very strong mutated person. It has a high field of view and vision/scent range. It deals very high damage and can take a lot of punishment before falling.

Tweeker
The tweeker is very similar to the wight, but it is much faster and harder to hit as it tweeks and jerks uncontrollably.

Common Afflicted
The common afflicted are very much like zombies. They retain their human appearance and traits but have a lust for blood and will stop at nothing to satisfy it.

Deranged
The deranged are another form of the common afflicted. They are just slightly more resistant to damage, and can use basic tools as weapons. They are mostly slow and not very intelligent.

Mongrel
The mongrel was a biogenetically altered creature that was an old Soviet project, revitalized by the authorities of the Triglav Complex. It is a mix of a human and a gene modified wolf. It is fast, damage resistant, and deals damage at a very high rate. It also has high vision/scent range but suffers from a very low field of view as it has very low peripheral vision.

Invalid
The invalid are the test subjects for the various human experiments at the Triglav Complex. They are slow, average in health, have low field of view and sight/scent distances. They are sickened by various illnesses and driven insane due to torture and numerous operations.

Most of the afflicted have several variants with varied stats and appearances.

This is not a complete list, but this gives everyone a look at what we have been working with so far. Please let us know what you think.

-[b]Corrosion[/b] :CStudios:

notes.title: Affliction - 7/17/17 Development Status Update/Demo Announcement
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

Hello followers of [i]Affliction[/i]!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28286649/b54f024ee0cff105e9c630526132127684905c51.png[/img]

I wanted to stop by with yet another status update going over what I accomplished today.

The third map is now completed with the exception of enemies and story items. Work on the fourth map has already begun. We have no idea how many maps will be in the final game but it'll be a lot. There are many plans in place for other maps to follow. We still have a very long way to go for mapping.

The firearms chambered round system is working exactly how we wanted now that we've worked a few kinks out.

We have completed sound sets for a few more npcs but we still need more sound effects to be sent in. If you want to participate in the community voice acting contest, please feel free to do so. Details for that can be found in the news/announcements section of this community hub.

We've decided to compile a very small section of the game and make it into a demo. We've never done one before, so this will be our first. Basically, it will just be a small segment of the main game without any progression features like moving from map to map or the usage of all the weapons. It will give potential customers a brief chance to see if their rig is up to the task of running the game and to see if it catches their interest. It won't be available for a few more days as it needs to be cleared by Valve, but it shouldn't be too long. It will come out as soon as possible. The demo is less than 500MB so it should be easily accessible to anyone.

At the rate that development is going, it won't be too much longer before the game is publicly released for Early Access and ready for players to start their fight against the tyrants and abominations that dwell in Ghulovka!

I'll be back with another status update as soon as I complete more items on my agenda. I'm trying to do one of these every day.

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

Weapons (firearms) now have a chambered round system. This means that when the weapon is reloaded but still has ammo in the magazine and a bullet in the chamber, the capacity increases by 1 to count the extra round temporarily. I added in hints throughout the first real level (after the intro) that act as a guide for players and also a bit of a tutorial. The intro will probably have these too. notes.title: Affliction - Community Voice Acting Contest
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

[b]Community Voice Acting Contest[/b]

Hello everyone!

So, I have been getting a lot of emails and questions regarding how people can contribute to the development of the game. I want to do a community voice acting contest that will give everyone a chance to take part in the development of [i]Affliction[/i].

---

[b]The Timeline:[/b]
The contest starts today, 7/10/17 and ends 7/30/17.

---

[b]The Requirements:[/b]

[u]Please read the following before recording:[/u] The recordings need to be short, from 1 - 3 seconds in length with 5 seconds being the absolute maximum. File types should be .wav/.ogg/.mp3/.m4a. Most computers nowadays have a built in voice recorder which should do the trick. Files should be named with the number on the corresponding list found in the link below. Before sending, please put the recordings into a single zipped file with winrar, 7zip, or just a standard windows zipped file folder.

Speak in a regular inside speech volume and try to eliminate background noises for the duration of the recordings. If you are able and willing, do a slight Eastern European accent. Try not to over do it, just have a slight vocal adjustment. If you don't want to do that, that [u]isn't[/u] a problem. Do not make your voice deeper, just speak in a normal voice. We'll be using a voice synthesizer to add effects. [u]Both male and female voices are needed![/u]

There is no set amount of entries, so if you want to participate, feel free. We'll listen to anything we get before the deadline. Please include a link to your steam profile and your steam nickname when you submit your entry. Entries without these will be disregarded. There is no guarantee your recordings will be used, but if you would like to send something in, you're more than welcome to do so.

You can find the phrases and vocal emotes that we need in the link below. Feel free to improvise and make slight changes to the phrase as we don't need a million of the same exact sound.

[b]Link:[/b]
https://pastebin.com/gc0XN7LP

Send recordings to [u]crsvstudiosspprt@gmail.com[/u]

---

[b]The Rewards:[/b]

Winners will get free keys to [i]Affliction[/i] and their name will appear in the credits. They will also have a chance to test play the game before anyone else! More rewards may follow such as free DLC keys for example.

---

[u]Please post questions or comments about this below in the comments section of this announcement. I'll monitor them incase anyone needs clarification on anything.[/u]

Please also post below if you plan to participate, if you don't mind.

I'll select several winners by the end date. I look forward to hearing what everyone sends! Remember, this is for fun! Don't stress!

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

notes.title: Affliction - 7/9/17 Development Status Update
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28286649/b54f024ee0cff105e9c630526132127684905c51.png[/img]

So, I have some good news!

Yesterday, I was able to get the AI to be able to completely move without needing player interaction. They can now wander, patrol, hunt, and so on. AI soldiers who see or hear something will now hunt for a semi random amount of time before returning to a calm state and returning to what they were previously doing.

I put some more work into fine tuning the weapons again too. I feel that the changes I made make the weapons have a bit more "impact" in the game. From physics force applied, to damage, to sounds. I'll have some video footage shortly for this. I recently invested in a video creation application that should help out a lot.

I have decided to implement a side healing system along side the health item pickups in the game. As of right now, the player regenerates 1 health every 15 seconds. That may increase but will likely not decrease. The game is meant to be more realistic but I found that the player will almost always have at least some damage and I wanted to add a way to slowly regain lost health. Health pickups will be common, but not to the point where you find one around every corner. Depending on feedback and community opinion, I may completely remove this later. For now, I think it adds a way to help players get along through the game.

The reason I felt it was a good idea to add the healing system is because the game is an action game before anything else. It has several sub-genres but it is an action game. Just health pickups would make some parts extremely difficult and require many attempts. This way, players at least have a chance. I feel it needs balance so people won't abuse it.

I'll continue to keep everyone posted. Please post comments and thoughts on this.

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

Yesterday, I was able to get the AI to be able to completely move without needing player interaction. They can now wander, patrol, hunt, and so on. AI soldiers who see or hear something will now hunt for a semi random amount of time before returning to a calm state and returning to what they were previously doing.

I put some more work into fine tuning the weapons again too. I feel that the changes I made make the weapons have a bit more "impact" in the game. From physics force applied, to damage, to sounds. I'll have some video footage shortly for this. I recently invested in a video creation application that should help out a lot.

I have decided to implement a side healing system along side the health item pickups in the game. As of right now, the player regenerates 1 health every 15 seconds. That may increase but will likely not decrease. The game is meant to be more realistic but I found that the player will almost always have at least some damage and I wanted to add a way to slowly regain lost health. Health pickups will be common, but not to the point where you find one around every corner. Depending on feedback and community opinion, I may completely remove this later. For now, I think it adds a way to help players get along through the game.

The reason I felt it was a good idea to add the healing system is because the game is an action game before anything else. It has several sub-genres but it is an action game. Just health pickups would make some parts extremely difficult and require many attempts. This way, players at least have a chance. I feel it needs balance so people won't abuse it.

I'll continue to keep everyone posted. Please post comments and thoughts on this.

-[b]Corrosion[/b] :CStudios:

notes.title: Affliction - Sound Overhaul Status Update
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

Hey everyone!

I wanted to post another quick status update about the work that I accomplished yesterday.

I finished up the ai code for all of the npcs ai in the game. This doesn't mean they won't be improved on or fixed if there are bugs in the future, it just means that they work well, and they do their job for the time being.

Another thing I took care of yesterday was the player sound effects. Footsteps now sound heavier and they give a real "boots on the ground" feeling. They make the game much more immersive than the old stock ones. I don't want anything stock, I want everything to be unique, so I'm going out of my way to do so. I'm hoping that when players hear the difference, they'll agree with me that they are much better.

Atmospheric sound effects have also been improved so they should give a much better immersive feel.

Within the next few weeks, I plan to do the voice acting and sound effects for the human npcs. I think those will turn out pretty well, as I have voice masking software which can do many different effects.

Weapon sound effects have been taken care of, but they still act a little strange now and then. The way the engine handles automatic fire is quite different so they will still be worked on.

Another thing I did was reduce overall movement speed slightly, and increase the footstep sound rate dramatically. Before I did this, the player moved very fast and footstep sounds were too far apart. Think of a person taking steps of about 5 feet long. Yes, it was bad. Now, they fit directly with the animation and speed of acceleration. To go with this, I also increased the camera wobble when moving but only slightly. I personally dislike games that over dramatize camera sway from movement so I did this very sparingly.

We're getting there, it really shouldn't be too much longer before I have something playable. Technically, I do now, but it isn't much. I need to complete more mapping first before I release anything. I hope you all understand why things are taking this long, I'm really trying to set this apart from the mass of other ([u]mostly[/u] sub-par) products from this engine.

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː

notes.title: Affliction - NPC & AI Status Update
notes.notes:
[b]Affliction[/b],

Hey everyone!

Today I had great success and got a ton of things accomplished. From finishing up the npc models, finishing the ai, almost completing the ai sound effects, to enhancing ai combat behavior and so on.

These were some things that have been on my to-do list for a very long time but now I can comfortably say that everything that has to do with the ai or npcs is almost completed. If I had to give an estimate, I'd say they are 90% fully completed.

As of right now, there are over 25 different human enemy types and over 25 different monsters to fight. They are not just retextured versions either. There are several distinct monster and human enemy "classes".

The stock ai that comes with the engine by default isn't the best, but it is decent, so I have been going through each and every script and changing the code to be much more reactive, smarter, and more challenging. I wanted to make it unique of course as well.

Enemies can react to sounds (not necessarily the player) and sight of course. They can also react to "situational awareness" like sitting behind an enemy while trying to sneak by but taking too long. 

Certain enemies also have a "territory" radius which will cause them to become aggravated if the player enters.

Human ai will use cover, patrol, suppress, and flank in order to create a realistic and challenging combat simulation.

Monster ai will use all sorts of different tactics to kill their prey including charging, sneaking, leaping, and even pretending to be dead in some cases.

One of the major things I wanted to focus on with [i]Affliction[/i] was sound effects. Since the graphics are not AAA quality, atmosphere and sound are extremely important in a game like this so I have gone out of my way to purchase and create dozens of sound effects that I feel will really serve the game well. I can't wait to show everyone!

I also finished up the HUD and made it look really good, if I do say so myself. It fits well with the theme of the game. I'll have pictures soon and new videos soon.

The last thing I wanted to mention was optimization. To help with performance and keep the game running smooth, I've made the decision to make slightly smaller maps, but make more of them. This will make it necessary to have more loading screens, but it'll reduce overall loading times, and also help keep a steady fps. I will continue to work on optimization and hope to further improve performance as time goes on.

[u]The game should be ready for Early Access players soon![/u]

As always, please stay tuned for more updates and let me know what you guys think.

-[b]Corrosion[/b] ːCStudiosː
